elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.intro
elements.html:
Distinguish explicit rules, learning from examples, and generative output without treating them as mutually exclusive eras.

Some software follows rules people specify. Machine learning fits patterns using data. Generative AI produces content such as text or images. These approaches coexist: a generative model can be machine learning, and a product can combine models with ordinary rules. Training adjusts a model using data; inference uses the trained model. A useful test asks how a system works, not just whether its label says AI.

Practice scenario

Three fictional tools: A sends a reminder when a timer reaches zero. B learns to label plant photos from labeled examples. C generates a new club announcement from a brief.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.teaching
elements.html:
Three approaches that still work together

A rule-based tool follows a condition a person wrote: if the timer reaches zero, show a reminder. A learned classifier fits patterns from examples, such as labeled plant photos. A generator produces content, such as a new announcement. These are overlapping descriptions, not a timeline where each new approach erases the last.

Training changes; inference uses

During training, a model is adjusted using data. When a trained plant model labels a new photo, it is doing inference. That one prediction does not prove the label is correct or mean the model learned from the photo. A product may separately collect data for later training; do not assume it does or does not.

Test beyond the examples it learned from

Imagine a fictional leaf classifier trained only on clear daylight photos. A useful test includes different photos with independently checked labels, including shade or unfamiliar backgrounds. Record which predictions match and which fail. Testing only the training examples can hide a model that learned those examples but performs poorly on new ones.

Your turn: design two tools

  1. On paper or in your own words, invent a rule with an explicit if/then condition. You do not need to code it.
  2. Invent a learned tool. Name the examples it would train on and the prediction it would make.
  3. Inspect the prediction table and save your error analysis. Then design two new test cases for your own learned tool, with expected answers and a way to check them.
  4. Save your designs and test plan in the final step. Use fictional objects or made-up club tasks; do not upload photos or personal data.

Can you explain why your test examples are separate from training? What would you do if the tool fails one?

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches
elements.title: Which explanation best matches the three fictional tools?

choices.text: A follows a rule; B learns labels; C follows fixed rules because its output is text.
A follows a rule; B learns labels; C generates text and can also learn patterns from data.
A learns from elapsed time; B follows fixed rules because people supplied its example labels.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.output
elements.html: Text output does not establish fixed rules. Generation describes the output, while learning describes how patterns are fitted.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.mix
elements.html: These descriptions can overlap: a generator can be a learned model, and a product can also use ordinary rules.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.approaches.feedback.input
elements.html: Receiving an input is not itself learning. In the brief, B fits patterns from labeled examples; A applies a specified timer rule.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.error_analysis
elements.title: Your analysis: identify the wrong prediction, the row that cannot count as a new-example test, one next test case, and a limit on what these results tell you.
elements.description: Self-review: Compare checked labels with predictions by row.; Separate reused training data from new test examples.; Propose another independently checked case; do not infer a general cause from one error.. Presence only; not automatically graded.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.prediction_review
elements.title: After your own analysis, which conclusion fits the table?

choices.text: B is wrong; the other three rows are successful new-example tests, so use those four to estimate reliability.
B is wrong; D reuses training data. Check more new examples before relying on the model.
B is wrong in shade; all shaded photos will fail, so daylight-only use is now proven safe.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.prediction_review.feedback.all_new
elements.html: D is reused training data. Do not count it as an independent new-example test; this tiny set is also insufficient to establish general reliability.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.prediction_review.feedback.limited
elements.html: B differs from its checked label. D cannot count as a new-example test. A and C match, but these few results do not establish general reliability.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.prediction_review.feedback.cause
elements.html: One shaded error does not prove its cause or predict every shaded result. Two daylight matches do not prove daylight use is safe.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check
elements.title: Can a generative system also use machine learning?

choices.text: No; they must be separate technologies.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check.feedback.yes
elements.html: Generation describes output, while learning describes how patterns are fitted.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.overlap_check.feedback.no
elements.html: A generative model can learn from data.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.transfer
elements.title: Invent a simple rule-based tool and a tool that learns from examples. State the rule’s condition and action, the learned tool’s training examples and prediction, and two NEW test cases. Explain how you would check expected answers, identify errors, and respond to a failed test.
elements.description: Practice text only. Saved on this device. Reviewed by you or an educator, not AI graded.

elements.name: lai.ai-you-can-use.l02.rubric
elements.html:
Self-check

  • Rule has an explicit condition and action.
  • Learning example identifies training data and a prediction.
  • Two test cases are separate from training, with independently checked expected answers.
  • Explains how a mismatch changes the use decision; avoids claiming the small test proves reliability.

Systems can combine approaches. Do not date a single clean switch from rules to learning or infer consciousness from outputs.
